messages:
sophia: quick summary from this morning's weight-only INT8 runs on orion-13b (trying both bitsandbytes and llm.int8 backends). rough numbers below, open questions after. :mag:

sophia: perf (p50 latency, batch=1, seq=512):
```
bnb/w-only: 41.8 ms
llm.int8: 36.9 ms
fp16: 59.2 ms
```

sophia: throughput (tokens/sec steady-state): `bnb: 1200`, `llm.int8: 1400`, `fp16: 850`

sophia: quality quick-check on our longform QA slice (1000 prompts): exact-match F1 drop vs fp16: `bnb: -0.9%`, `llm.int8: -1.6%` (mostly on math/precision prompts)

sophia: latency distribution shows llm.int8 has tighter tail (p95 2x smaller than bnb). bnb had a few 200–400ms spikes correlated with multi-request batching on the bench harness.

raj: nice, can you paste the bench command and docker image tag? want to repro locally.

sophia: sure:
```
./bin/bench --model orion-13b --quant weightonly --backend llmint8 --batch 1 --seq 512 --seed 42
docker: registry/redwood/orion:2026-03-15-ev1
```

kevin: are we sure the quality delta is statistically significant? 1000 prompts is small for longtail. maybe run the 10k eval slice. also need to check temperature/aggressive sampling differences.

maria: I pushed a 10k slice to S3: `s3://redwood-evals/orion/w-only-10k-2026-03-15.jsonl` — it's the same golden prompts used in prior rollout.

emily: FYI I hit a segfault on one node when falling back to CPU for a particular request pattern (many short sequences back-to-back). stack trace points at bnb_cuda kernel on mixed-batch path.

kevin: @emily can you attach the node id + logs? we should mark that as P1 for Dedicated clusters. if that's reproducible it's a hard block for auto-fallback.

emily: node: i-0f9b2c7a, logs uploaded to `/var/log/redwood/bench/segfault-2365129.log`. repro script in the gist: https://gist.github.com/emily/4a2f9 

raj: question on tokenizer alignment — did we use the same tokenizer/merges across fp16 and int8 artifacts? small tokenization differences can explain skew on numeric QA.

sophia: yes same tokenizer binary, same vocabulary sha256 `a1b2c3...`. I also fixed the prompt normalization to strip trailing whitespace.

kevin: suggested canary rollout plan: 1) internal e2e tests + 10k eval baseline compare; 2) 1% traffic -> monitor rouge/qa metrics and latency; 3) 5% with autoscale + fallback to fp16 on >1% degradation in QA. fallback implemented at routing layer. thoughts?

maria: add a synthetic adversarial slice (edge numbers, nested lists) — when I ran earlier, llm.int8 had most failures on nested arithmetic. I uploaded slice: `s3://redwood-evals/orion/adversarial-nests-2k.jsonl`.

sophia: note on cost: int8 variants reduce token cost per second by ~45% (GPU utilization improvements + lower memory footprint). That's our biggest win if quality delta is acceptable.

ci-bot: CI: int8-quality-regression test failed on PR #4123 — "orion longform QA RMSE increased by 1.8% (threshold 1.0%)."

kevin: thanks CI. that's the exact failure margin we suspected. need to triage whether it's bnb implementation or quantization math.

raj: two quick hypotheses: 1) per-channel scale vs per-tensor scale differences between backends; 2) KV-cache attention accumulation numeric drift. both can cause small deltas.

sophia: plan: run a deterministic micro-eval focusing on attention math diffs (same seed, same batched vs unbatched executions) and then run a token-by-token diff tool to see where outputs diverge.

emily: I'll reproduce the segfault on an isolated box and try the llm.int8 backend there as well. if bnb segfaults only, that narrows scope.

maria: ops-bot — can you schedule a canary window for Thursday 03:00–07:00 UTC and reserve 4 infer nodes?

ops-bot: scheduled maintenance window and canary slot for 2026-03-19 03:00–07:00 UTC. Reserved nodes: infer-raw-04..07. Notifications sent to #eng-oncall. :white_check_mark:

kevin: good. action items:
- sophia: run 10k eval and token-diff (due EOD)
- emily: reproduce segfault and upload crash dump (ASAP)
- raj: micro-eval on attention accumulation (tomorrow)
- maria: prepare canary slice + alert thresholds (tomorrow)

sophia: ack — running the longer eval now, will post results in this thread. attaching interim table: 
```
metric,bnb,llm.int8,fp16
EM_F1,87.3,86.6,88.1
ROUGE-L,74.2,73.8,75.0
p50_ms,41.8,36.9,59.2
p95_ms,120.4,78.3,180.9
```

raj: interesting p95 difference. llm.int8 looks better for tail which helps interactive UX. bnb's p95 spike is concerning for small bursty requests.

maria: if the longform QA delta stays within 1% after 10k, I'm fine with starting 1% canary and strict rollback. if >1.5% we hold.

kevin: agreed. also include fallback path tests in the canary — simulated quality regression that triggers immediate routing to fp16.

sophia: will add an eval hook that computes rolling delta and a canary health signal (json payload) to the console dashboard.

emily: uploaded crash dump and a minimal repro harness: `s3://redwood-debug/segfaults/orion-bnb-2365129.tar.gz`

kevin: ok team — keep follow-ups here. if anyone finds a quick mitigation (per-channel re-scaling, small quant bias correction) drop it here and we'll try it in the lab build. :rocket:"
